semanticEvidence.finding: CostSacrificeSelf is the source permanent; CostTap is source tap; CostComposite stores multiple costs. AtomSacrifice defaults count=1 and excludeSelf=false; AtomMana carries mana cost; AtomPayLife carries a nonnegative fixed amount for Greed.
semanticEvidence.basis: ActivatedAbility.kt AbilityCost subtypes around lines 463-640 and 752-765; CostAtom.kt Mana/PayLife/Sacrifice declarations.

semanticEvidence.finding: Composite affordability uses costs.all; payment iterates each subcost, propagating state and mana pool and stopping on failure. These exports therefore represent conjunction, not choice.
semanticEvidence.limitation: Same-initial-state component affordability is not a general proof of arbitrary shared-resource composites. No such broader completeness claim is made.

semanticEvidence.finding: SacrificeSelf affordability requires source on battlefield and projected controller equals payer. Normal activation validator checks source controller through projected state. Self-sacrifice payment moves sourceId itself. It does not consult sacrificedPermanents as a substitute source.
semanticEvidence.limitation: Low-level payAbilityCost is not independently a full legality validator. SacrificeSelf payment itself lacks the same battlefield/payer recheck present in affordability; controller/zone permission claims rely on the enclosing validated activation path.

semanticEvidence.finding: Creature filter is CardPredicate.IsCreature. Candidates come from controlledBattlefield and projected predicate matching. paySacrificeList rechecks selected permanent is on battlefield, projected controlled by payer, matches filter, and respects excludeSelf. Viscera Seer default count is one, excludeSelf false.
semanticEvidence.basis: ObjectFilter.kt line 216; CostAtom.kt lines 162-170; CostHandler.kt lines 714-723, 1154-1248 and 1814-1825.
semanticEvidence.limitation: controlledBattlefield and predicate evaluator implementation were not separately traced; selected payment contains explicit controller and battlefield backstops.

semanticEvidence.finding: Both self and selected sacrifices delegate to moveToZone(entityId, GRAVEYARD) and mark sacrifice. ZoneTransitionService obtains ownerId from CardComponent and builds nonbattlefield destination ZoneKey(ownerId, actualDestZone). It obtains last-known controller from projected state for battlefield exits. Thus owner-destination and sacrifice-controller are separate actual code paths, not inferred from the serialized filter.
semanticEvidence.basis: CostHandler.kt lines 422-438 and 1230-1245; ZoneTransitionService.kt lines 275-286 and 410-428.
semanticEvidence.limitation: actualDestZone can be redirected by replacement processing. Replacement ordering, commander choices, tokens and control-change cleanup need execution; these provisions establish the normal routing intent, not observed correctness for every replacement.

semanticEvidence.finding: Greed encodes a fixed 2-life atom and black mana separately. checkLifeCostPayable runs for every payment strategy. Shared affordability reaches GameState.canPayLife, which accepts lifeTotal >= amount and checks payment prohibitions. CostHandler delegates actual payment to LifePaymentService.
semanticEvidence.basis: ActivationValidator.kt checkLifeCostPayable; CostHandler.kt lines 706-713 and 862-867; CostAtomAmounts.kt lines 106-112; GameState.kt lines 1247-1272.
semanticEvidence.limitation: LifePaymentService implementation and state-based loss sequence were not traced or executed. Exact subtraction and paying-to-zero outcome require execution; serialized amount and >= threshold are directly evidenced.

semanticEvidence.finding: Composite tap costs exclude sourceId from mana solver sources. Payment excludes sourceId from both auto and explicit selected mana sources when the outer ability has a tap cost. This preserves Mind Stone draw cost distinction: its own tap-for-mana cannot alone fund its draw while paying another tap.
semanticEvidence.basis: ActivationValidator.kt canPayAbilityCostWithSources; ActivationCostPayer.kt activateManaAbilities around lines 420-457.
semanticEvidence.limitation: Mana solver, auto-tapper and restricted-mana correctness were not executed or comprehensively inspected.

semanticEvidence.finding: With more legal sacrifice candidates than count, activation pauses for SelectCardsDecision with min=max=1 for Viscera Seer. SubmitDecision checks player and decision ID, validator checks offered options and count. Sacrifice resumer checks count and stored candidates, fills AdditionalCostPayment.sacrificedPermanents and reenters handler.execute. Selected objects are rechecked by paySacrificeList.
semanticEvidence.basis: ActivationChoicePauses.kt lines 380-419; ActivateAbilityXCostContinuationResumer.kt lines 248-288; SubmitDecisionHandler.kt lines 23-58; DecisionValidators.kt lines 285-315.
semanticEvidence.limitation: A pause is unfinished work, not payment success or failure. Entire round trip and invalid response rollback remain unexecuted.

semanticEvidence.finding: Outcome distinguishes Done, Paused and Rejected. ActionProcessor restores the exact input state on rejected actions and removes attempted events, including execution failures after intermediate immutable work. Handler-direct results are not identical to public transactional guarantees.
semanticEvidence.basis: ActionProcessor.kt lines 77-104; Outcome.kt and ExecutionResult.kt declarations.
semanticEvidence.limitation: Read-only semantic evidence. No failure, rollback or continuation was executed.

semanticEvidence.finding: SDK defaults are instant-speed timing, nonmana ability and battlefield activation. Mind Stone:1 explicitly sets ManaAbility/true. Handler pays before routing mana abilities to immediate resolver or nonmana abilities to putOnStack. Exported drawing/discard/search/scry instructions are effects, distinct from cost.
semanticEvidence.basis: ActivatedAbility.kt lines 44, 46, 75; ActivateAbilityHandler.kt executeActivation stages 3 and 5.
semanticEvidence.limitation: Individual effect executors, stack target revalidation and full resolution are outside this native-payment review.

implementationConcerns.sourceRequirement: A source already tapped cannot pay its tap-symbol activation cost (frozen Phase A: 107.5, 118.3, 701.26a).
evidence: ActivationValidator.checkCostPayable returns null immediately for PaymentStrategy.Explicit (line 505); checkExplicitPaymentSources checks the listed mana sources, not independently the outer ability source tap payment.
CostHandler.payAbilityCost AbilityCost.Tap calls tap and unconditionally returns success; no affordability call appears at the start of payAbilityCost.
TapHelpers.tap returns unchanged state and no tap event when the source is already tapped (lines 114-117).
ActivateAbilityHandler adds an already-tapped guard only when lockedCost != null (around lines 187-191). Ordinary explicit submitted activations use the default lockedCost=null path.
For Mind Stone:2, existing floating mana or another selected legal mana source can satisfy the mana component without addressing the already-tapped outer source.
implementationConcerns.assessment: The inspected chain appears to permit an explicit activation with an already-tapped source while paying no actual tap. This is an implementation-path concern despite correct printed serialized costs. It is not a runtime observation or an executed counterexample.
proposedFreshProbe: Submit each affected native ability through ActionProcessor with source initially tapped and PaymentStrategy.Explicit; supply adequate floating/other-source mana for Mind Stone:2. Expect rejection with unchanged state, no sacrifice or stack ability, and no extra mana.
Compare with otherwise identical untapped-source legal control and AutoPay tapped-source negative control. Record outcome, state, events, zone movement, source tap state and stack or mana result.
Keep direct handler calls separate from public ActionProcessor guarantees; do not infer rejection solely from absence of a tap event.
